reason: The provided sources contain sufficient overlapping facts to support an engaging short-form video script with over 10 verified claims.
story: In March 1989, a 300-meter asteroid named 4581 Asclepius crossed Earth's orbital path. It passed through the exact region our planet had occupied just six hours earlier. At the time, nobody knew it had happened. Astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas only discovered the asteroid nine days after the close encounter, spotting it at California's Palomar Observatory. Passing at a distance of roughly 684,000 kilometers, the near-miss served as a major wake-up call regarding our blind spots in detecting potentially hazardous space rocks. Geophysicists estimated that a direct hit would have released energy comparable to a 600-megaton atomic bomb, capable of regional devastation. The terrifying close call helped drive the creation of modern planetary defense programs to track threats before they fly past unseen.
angle: A 300-meter city-killer asteroid missed Earth by a mere six hours in 1989, and astronomers completely missed it until nine days after it had already flown past.

claims.claim: Asteroid 4581 Asclepius is approximately 300 meters in diameter.
The asteroid passed Earth on March 22, 1989.
Asclepius passed Earth at a distance of roughly 684,000 kilometers (425,000 miles).
The asteroid crossed Earth's orbital path just six hours after Earth was at that location.
Astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas discovered the asteroid.
The discovery was made at Palomar Observatory in California.
The asteroid was discovered on March 31, 1989, nine days after its closest approach.
A collision with Asclepius was estimated to release energy comparable to a 600-megaton atomic bomb.
Asclepius is classified as an Apollo asteroid and a potentially hazardous asteroid.
The near-miss helped drive the creation of modern asteroid tracking and planetary defense programs.
The asteroid's orbital period is approximately 378 days (or 1.03 years).
The asteroid will make a future close pass on March 24, 2051.

disputed: Source S4 lists Jean Mueller as a co-discoverer alongside Henry Holt, while S1, S3, and S5 credit Norman Thomas. Scripts should attribute Thomas or stick to the consensus of Holt and Thomas found in the majority of sources.
